# zsytrf_aa

> Computes the factorization of a complex symmetric matrix using Aasen's algorithm (blocked).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zsytrfAa from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zsytrf_aa';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zsytrf_aa( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, IPIV, strideIPIV, WORK ) → integer
```

Computes the factorization of a complex symmetric matrix `A` using Aasen's algorithm (blocked).

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input/output symmetric matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | pivot index output array, length `N` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, 2 * N )` |  | caller-provided workspace (length at least `max(1,2*N)`, the reference's minimum; a length of at least `N*(1+NB)` with `NB` from `ilaenv` (64) enables the full block size, and a shorter one a smaller block size); `null` allocates the optimal size `max(1,N*(1+NB))` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

  On exit, the tridiagonal matrix is stored in the diagonals and the subdiagonals of A just below (or above) the diagonals, and L is stored below (or above) the subdiagonals, when `UPLO` is 'L' (or 'U').
- `IPIV`: On exit, it contains the details of the interchanges, i.e., the row and column k of A were interchanged with the row and column `IPIV(k)`.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `0`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zsytrf_aa.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Computes the factorization of a complex symmetric matrix `A` using Aasen's algorithm (blocked).

The form of the factorization is `A = U^T*T*U` (upper) or `A = L*T*L^T` (lower),
where `T` is a complex symmetric tridiagonal matrix.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | input/output symmetric matrix (column-major) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for `A` (in complex elements) |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | pivot index output array, length `N` |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `IPIV` |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for `IPIV` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, 2 * N )` |  | caller-owned workspace (length from `offsetWork` at least `max(1,2*N)`, the reference's minimum, when `N > 0`; a length of at least `N*(1+NB)` with `NB = 64` (from `ilaenv`) enables the full block size, and a shorter one a block size of `floor((length-N)/N)`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `WORK` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | index offset for `WORK` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the symmetric matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

  On exit, the tridiagonal matrix is stored in the diagonals and the subdiagonals of A just below (or above) the diagonals, and L is stored below (or above) the subdiagonals, when `UPLO` is 'L' (or 'U').
- `IPIV`: On exit, it contains the details of the interchanges, i.e., the row and column k of A were interchanged with the row and column `IPIV(k)`.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: `0`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK must be sufficiently large

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0` or `N === 1`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zsytrf_aa()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZSYTRF_AA`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zsytrf_aa.f).
-   `IPIV` stores standard 0-based pivot indices. Aasen's algorithm does NOT use
    the Bunch-Kaufman negative-IPIV encoding (unlike `zsytrf`, `zsytrf_rk`, or
    `zsytrf_rook`).
-   On exit, the complex symmetric tridiagonal `T` is stored on the diagonals of `A`
    (with sub/superdiagonal stored adjacent), and `L` (or `U`) is stored below
    (or above) the subdiagonals.
-   The block size `NB` comes from `ilaenv` (64), as in the reference.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zsytrfAa from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zsytrf_aa';

// 4x4 complex symmetric matrix (column-major lower-triangular layout):
const A = new Complex128Array( 16 );
const IPIV = new Int32Array( 4 );

A.set( [ 4, 0.1 ], 0 );
A.set( [ 2, -0.2 ], 1 );
A.set( [ 1, 0.3 ], 2 );
A.set( [ 5, -0.1 ], 5 );
A.set( [ 2, 0.4 ], 6 );
A.set( [ 1, 0.0 ], 7 );
A.set( [ 6, 0.2 ], 10 );
A.set( [ 3, -0.3 ], 11 );
A.set( [ 8, 0.1 ], 15 );

const info = zsytrfAa( 'column-major', 'lower', 4, A, 4, IPIV, 1, null );

console.log( 'info: %d', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'IPIV: %s', IPIV ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZSYTRF_AA`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZSYTRF\_AA computes the factorization of a complex symmetric matrix A using the Aasen's algorithm. The form of the factorization is

$$
A = U^T \, T \, U \quad\text{or}\quad A = L \, T \, L^T
$$

where U (or L) is a product of permutation and unit upper (lower) triangular matrices, and T is a complex symmetric tridiagonal matrix.

This is the blocked version of the algorithm, calling Level 3 BLAS.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
